But what now is -- we established all that yesterday, I think it was. What is the issue especially about this latter part? Because a lot of attention was paid yesterday to whether, on the 6th, such a committee attended the scene. But what now is the issue, again, going through this ambiguity in the text? What do we have to understand from this repeated -- that since there is no clear refusal on all levels to participate, that from this letter, we cannot conclude that UNPROFOR was not there on the 6th. Is that what you are seeking to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's clear to me. It was clear to me yesterday as well, but if -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we also want to draw Your Honours' attention is that there is a document, P538, also shown to the witness yesterday, from which it is clear that UNPROFOR took part in this investigation. And we know from the record of this case that UNPROFOR did take part in this investigation. And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I need to have another look at P538. I'll do that. Please proceed meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can call on our screens P538.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I can -- if you have any further questions for the witness, okay; but if not, I'll just look at 538. I don't need to have it on the screen because I've got my own screen, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, but I want that document to follow up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. If you have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're interested in item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gengo, in item 5, it reads that members of the commission referred to here, meaning that it is not the commission we discussed of the 6th but another UNPROFOR commission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber was on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was just going to -- I believe Mr. Lukic just quickly corrected himself. I was going to object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, if that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I haven't finished the question yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this commission referred to in this document and this document were offered as evidence, and it does not record the visit of a commission on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am going to object to the word "commission." I don't see where that appears in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you please put to the witness literally the portion you draw his attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here "the investigation team." I assume that there are several members involved, if it's called a team. In item 5, it says that members of that team arrived in Sarajevo on the 10th of February. Is it clear from this document that this team that is arriving only on the 10th could not have recorded anything that happened on the 6th of February?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- what exactly -- team members arrived. What team are we talking about exactly, Mr. Lukic? Could you guide me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In -- in -- in -- under number 3, it says composition -- the composition of the investigation team --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the investigation team, yes, yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- is shown in Annex A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what was put to you was that on page -- just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's page 40 in e-court. [In English] Is it page 40 in English version? On the screen? Because I have ERN number, four digits, 4137. No, we have to see the ERN number to be able to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seems to be last four digits 4752. And we have two ERN numbers on it. One at the bottom which is 4132 and the other one is at the top which is an R number, 4752.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have moved forward five pages. The fifth page after this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then 45 obviously. That's the page we need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There at the bottom of the page we find the last four digits, 4137, and at the top, 4757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have the corresponding page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the right one. There are two translations in e-court in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I can read the English paragraph. Actually, only the top part of the fourth paragraph, so we don't need a translation. The witness can hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read this out to you after I tell you what it is. The Prosecution pointed out yesterday that the commission that you spoke about did not go out and this is what this document says. I quote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: So it's the last paragraph here in the B/C/S version. You'll see it here on the left-hand side. It says: "Colonel Cvetkovic then discussed numerous aspects of the incident in theoretical terms and offered his personal opinion concerning the validity of events as portrayed by the media. He had no specific evidence to offer of direct relevance to the investigation." In this way also an effort was made to show that there was no such commission. Now let us look at document ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is approximately time for the break, but I wouldn't interrupt Mr. Lukic in the middle of what seems to be a question which is related to several documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: I would not interrupt you at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five minutes, probably, even less, to finish this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's -- let's finish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] So -- [In English] 65 ter number 18907. [Interpretation] Actually, this is what it says. Cvetkovic is providing an explanation why -- I mean, it's the paragraph underneath number 5. It says: "Members of the commission" -- so he is calling this team "the commission." It says here underneath paragraph number 5: "Members of the commission asked me as the representative of the VRS to provide technical details showing that the Serb side had not fired" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The English page is not the right page. It's the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we have a numbering starting twice. Perhaps we go to the next page in English and see whether it's the second series number 5 that you were reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, in B/C/S it's correct page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's then a -- well, then could we move further down in B/C/S. Move to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the English it's in the middle of the page. You can see it: "... as a representative of the VRS ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's -- yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Below the 5, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't consider that to be 5. 5 starts for me with the stabilising fin. Below 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Below 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what it says further on -- [In English] The next paragraph in English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Because the information on the explosion site was not available to me (the width and depth of the crater, the position of the stabilizing fin the direction and angle of descent), I tried to find out about it in informal conversations." And then number one says: "The commission did not determine with certainty the direction from which the shell was launched." Number 2: "On the basis of the position of the stabilising fin, which was removed on the first day, the angle of descent was not determined with precision, which is why the commission could not establish the exact launching distance." He goes on enumerating. Now, at the time, were you aware of this; namely that the Serb side had not been provided with information about the investigation taking place at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO GENGO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd just like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before ... Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 18907 receives number D481, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then you kept the witness busy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we cannot but follow and have no questions for the witness either. Mr. Gengo, this completes your testimony in this court. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Mr. Stojanovic, you'll examine the next witness. No protective measures, 92 ter, Mr. Maletic. Mr. Weber.

utterances.text: Your Honours, just consistent with our past discussions, I just want to inform the Chamber that the witness has been admonished pursuant to Rule 90(E) in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the record. Could the next witness be escorted in the courtroom. Yes, I think we discussed the matter. We leave it in the hands of the calling party whether or not to inform the witness about his rights under Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Maletic. Before you give evidence, you're invited to make a solemn declaration, the text of which is handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated, Mr. Maletic. Mr. Maletic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Maletic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to tell the Trial Chamber whether you provided a statement to the Mladic Defence and did you provide it in a written form?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to call up 1D01606 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the first page of the document together. Mr. Maletic, is this your signature, and is this information about you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's go to the last page of the same document. The statement is eight pages long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, my question is the same. Is this a confirmation that you provided a statement containing eight pages to the Mladic Defence, and did you sign it on the 10th of May, 2014?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours, I would like to call up 65 ter 1D03341. We made some minor changes and additions to the statement that this witness has provided. With your leave, I would like to briefly ask the witness the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, did you talk to me during the preparations for your testimony, and did you sign the addendum to the statement to which you made some minor changes yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 26 of your original statement, it is stated, inter alia, that the sentence: "There were no residential buildings in that area, save for two residential buildings." Your amendment to that sentence was: "Except for several smaller apartment buildings." We're talking about paragraph 26. My question is this: Why did you change your statement after the 10th of May when you signed it? Why did you ask us yesterday to replace the words "two buildings" by the words "several smaller buildings"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Well, I just happened to pass through that part of the building and I realised that there were not just two smaller buildings but several smaller apartment buildings there. And after that -- or, rather, I passed through that part of the building after I signed the original statement and that's why I asked you to make the -- that correction to the original statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now in paragraph 32 of your original statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make a pause, Mr. Stojanovic, between answer and question, and could I invite you also to make a small pause between question and answer. Otherwise, the interpreters will not be able to interpret the overlapping speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall do our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 32 of your original statement, inter alia, the following sentence has been added: "During a truce in 1994, two children were killed at Soping." Yesterday, in a conversation with me, you wanted me to add the following words: "Two children were killed, namely Milica Lalovic and Natasa Sucur." My question is this: How come that after the 10th of May, when you signed the original statement, you came by the specific information with regard to the names of the two children that you mentioned in -- in your original statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: In a conversation with my colleague who also testified here, I learned the names of the two children and that's why I wanted you to add those names to my original statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask for additional clarification. Could you give us the name of the person who told us you the names of the two girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Predrag Trapara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Maletic, if I were to ask you the same questions today, the same ones that our investigators put to you when you signed the original statement, with the additions that have you mentioned here today and after you have made the -- have taken the solemn declaration, would your answers be the same? And would your answers constitute the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, in the expectation that the statement and the additional statement will be tendered, could you provide numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1606 receives number D482. And document 1D3341 receives number D483, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D482 and D483 are admitted into evidence. Witness, could you tell us also when exactly you spoke -- and the question comes from in front of you, when did you exactly speak to -- to Mr. Trapara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it was on the 17th of this month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 17th. Was that the day when you had arrived, or the day after that, or the day after that? Do you remember why you know it was the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A day after my arrival, I met up with Predrag Trapara. We had an informal conversation, and I learned that during that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's not your personal knowledge. It's just that he knows the names and you repeat it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was aware of their killing but I didn't know their names. He only told me their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, whenever you say something in this court which is not your personal knowledge but what you heard from others, would you always clearly indicate what stems from your own memory, your own observation, and what stems from what you were told. Because adding the names here, it's not clear to us that you got it from someone else, and we always would like to know what you know by yourself and what others have told you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. And now I would like to tender the following documents pursuant to 65 ter, and they all accompany the witness's statement. The first one is 65 ter 1D02005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. But Mr. Weber has not jumped up yet. He now has.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was going to wait until Mr. Stojanovic says all of them and then I do have an objection on one and I believe one has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stojanovic, if you would just proceed with all the numbers until Mr. Weber jumps up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, our objection would be on the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It would be on 1D02005. It's on the basis of relevance. We see that this is a newspaper article dated 8 April 2010. It's the Prosecution's position that this document has little probative value to this Chamber based on its date and remoteness to the events, and it is very briefly commented upon if -- if barely at all by the witness in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I also noticed, and in the statement the witness just tells him -- tells you that he was shown a document. He doesn't say anything about the document. That's the newspaper article, I take it, that's ... relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness mentions that in paragraph 5 of his statement, and he says that he learned of that crime in the media, and that like most of the population of Sarajevo, he learned about that as something that preceded the beginning of war and war conflicts in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I hope that we will not have to hear witnesses telling us what they read in the media. But, at the same time, Mr. -- is there any dispute about the issue that policeman Pero Petrovic was killed at his workplace in the Novo Sarajevo police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is aware of his death and the date of it. We dispute the account that's given in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The account being?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, this -- I believe this article for pages discusses the event and how it happened. So do not believe this witness has the foundation to be talking about this. It's just the -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic told us that the witness learned about it from the media. He therefore, I take it, cannot confirm any details about -- apart from what he read in the media, which may not be the right source. At the same time, you may have heard that the Prosecution does not disagree that Pero Petrovic, the name is accurate. The place where he was killed, the Sarajevo police station, is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd have to specifically check, but we do have some information on it and when it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- do you -- under those circumstances do you still insist on tendering, Mr. Stojanovic? Then, of course, the Chamber will further consider and decide. Or would you like to wait until Mr. Weber has verified name, time, and the place where the person was killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. I would like Mr. Weber to check if any of this is incorrect, and maybe we will have stipulations about these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And "any of this," you mean what the witness says about it. Because you have heard already that the Prosecution disagrees with further details as presented in the exhibit or in the article. Okay. We'll wait. We leave it for the time being. We'll not yet mark it for identification. Mr. Weber, we would like to hear from you, or from you, together with Mr. Stojanovic, as soon as possible. Next one, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender the rest of the documents, by your leave, as it seems to me the best way to save time. I tender the following 65 ter documents: 1D02092, 1D02093, 1D02094, 1D02095, and 1D02029.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections. But the Prosecution notes that its records indicate that 1D02029 has already been admitted as Prosecution Exhibit P4445.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that what now remains are the others which are all maps marked by the witness. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2092 receives number D484. Document 1D2093 receives number D485. Document 1D2094 receives number D486. And document 1D2095 receives number D487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you repeat the first 1D number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2092 receives number D484.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now sometimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the 0 between the 1D and the following number is not always. But D484 up to and including D487 are admitted -- 6. Let me just check. No, D487 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. By your leave, Your Honour, I'd like to read out a summary of Mr. Maletic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the war broke out, the witness lived in Grbavica with his family. When the 1st Romanija Brigade, later to become the 1st Sarajevo Brigade, was established, he was appointed to the position as the commander of the 1st Company, 3rd Battalion. He held that position until late 1992 when he was transferred to the 3rd Battalion command to the position of assistant battalion commander for intelligence affairs. He stayed in that position until early 1994. During the war, his unit carried out predominantly defensive actions and commanded the view of a small part of town from its positions. The witness claims that his unit never opened fire, especially sniper fire, on civilians from the defence sector of his company. Throughout the war they were under the orders of the superior command, forbidding any action aimed at civilians. They were also frequently ordered not to open fire at all, thus, sustaining losses which would have been less had they been able to respond to enemy fire immediately. The witness will testify that the ABiH unit which engaged them had snipers and that they were posted in different civilian buildings. That information originated from different sources, such as interviews with defectors, intelligence, and, in particular, the fact that many civilians were killed deep within the settlements of Grbavica and Vrace. In addition to obtaining information from defectors, he also concluded that the enemy had snipers because there was always individual shooting during lulls. It always meant that snipers from parts of town under Muslim control were targeting selected targets on the VRS side. The witness will further point out that the enemy did not select targets and that it did not matter to the enemy side whether fighters or civilians would be hit. It resulted in many civilian inhabitants of Grbavica being killed. That is the summary of the witness's statement. Next, could we have in e-court document P3, page 24. I would like to get a more precise description of the positions held by the units to which Mr. Maletic belonged -- unit to which Mr. Maletic belonged.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, while we are waiting for the document, I wanted to tell that you are about to see a photograph. I know, as well as the Chamber knows, that you previously used a map with far less detail than we can see on this photograph in order to mark the positions of your unit. Given the fact that you describe the positions of your unit in the statement, kindly use the marker provided by the usher to indicate the positions of the unit commanded by you as company commander in 1992, at least to the extent we can see in the photograph. Please start with -- on the right-hand side and the first building where we could find your positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marking will be done in blue, Mr. Stojanovic, or what ... oh, yes, I see it started [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. I think it will be easy to see then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, sir, please continue drawing the line, describing at the same time what you are doing, and tell us, please, what the first building was where your unit was deployed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: This was the building of Invest Banka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Next we have the student dorm. And there was another position here between the sky-scraper and the student dorm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do stop there for a moment. The witness circled the place he just referred to. Kindly tell the Court, for the record, what kind of position it was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: It was a dugout with approaching trenches in order to have a position just between the sky-scraper and the student dorm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to get up, Your Honours -- -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- but I'm a bit confused as what we're -- which marking, because the witness has made many, are we referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were invited to mark the positions. What you are apparently doing is to mark a line or is -- could you explain exactly what the line represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The building of Invest Banka is 1-3. Then the student dorm. Then the position between the student dorm and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. 1-3. What is 1-3? I don't see any 1-3 on my screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The building of Invest Banka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see in this picture is that some numbers appear and that one building is marked in red 10; whereas the -- the 10 in the white box refers to former Invest Banka building. When referred to 1-3, did you refer to the building which is marked in red number 10?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I apologise Your Honour. I had mind the three Metalka buildings. The building of Invest Banka was not held by my unit. It was held by the battalion next to us, so I misspoke. I had the Metalka buildings in mind, 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now what we see on this picture is a red square marking with number 8 on it, and that comprises a large construction. And we read in the white box that that is the Metalka building. First of all, would that Metalka building, would that be a building in which you had any position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now I understand that to the right of that, where you seem to have marked a 1, and to the left of that, where you seem to have marked a 3, are these three, what you call, together, the Metalka buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, that's what we called them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you have positions in all three of these buildings or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the blue line which is at the side of the buildings we are looking at is not demonstrating where you were and where the others were because the buildings are still buildings - the Metalka buildings - which -- in which you had positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the blue line effectively is at the other side of these buildings then separating you from the other warring party?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first -- no, no, I'm still seeking confirmation. So is that correctly understood, that the line of separation would be at the other side of the buildings, which, of course, we cannot see? Or was it a river there? Or what was the line of separation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The river was behind the building and it was the separation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, apart from the three buildings where you wrote 1, 2, and 3 in blue, there's also a building with a red roof. Could you tell us what that building is and whether you had any positions in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the student dorm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the student dorm. And you had positions in that student dorm as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you marked a dot to the left of the students' dorm at the corner of what is another red square marking. That blue dot depicts what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the sky-scraper and the student dorm, around the middle, there was a trench that was dug in a meadow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. All the markings are clear to me now. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, let us continue, please. The next square contains four tall buildings. Can you use the blue marker to show whether your company line defence extended between those buildings.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Our trenches were at the foot of the high-rises.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the foot facing the river or was it at the foot facing the Grbavica area, at least the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the foot turned towards the river, towards the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So that's seen from here behind the building. Behind the buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Court, in order have a full picture of the situation, and perhaps use approximately dozens or hundreds of metres to tell us how far your lines stretched down the Miljacka river beyond the edge of this photograph. How far did the positions of your company reach?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Several hundred metres, to the next bridge called Bratsvo i Jedinstvo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Kindly place today's date on the photograph, which is the 28th of May, and sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need -- it can be tendered as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I seek to tender this photograph into evidence. I have additional two questions with regard to it, hence, do leave it on the screen for the time building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 24 of Exhibit P3 as marked by the witness receives number D488, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D488 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, let me ask you this: When you said that in the buildings in front of you, which you marked with the numbers 1, 2, and 3 in blue, you had positions, were those positions at some of the higher floors of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No. Those positions were at the foot of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you explained your deployment concerning the building in the red square bearing the number 9, did you, as the company, have any positions on one of the upper floors of that building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you have positions only on the ground floor of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: For personal safety. We were safer at the -- the bottom of those buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Maletic. We -- I have no further questions for you, and I would kindly ask you to provide answers as best you can to the Prosecutor as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Weber, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Maletic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution, and you'll find him to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Maletic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to pick up with the area that we were just discussing with respect to your zone of responsibility. In paragraph 8 of your statement, you describe the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Romanija Brigade. And I'm sorry to stop my question here, but, sir, do you have some documents in front of you at the witness stand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have this statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- if it is a clean copy, I do not know if you have any problems, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have not seen it. If I could just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it a clean copy of your statement? Could you -- could the usher just have a look at it and give it to Mr. Weber so that he can see whether it's with or without annotations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do see there's some markings on it. If I can check it over the next break and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then we rather ask the witness: Whatever you need from your statement, if you have to read it yourself, that it can always be shown on the screen, if need be, and there is a lot of handwriting on it. Would you please put it away and not consult it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, we do have a clean copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- if he needs it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- usually we don't -- if there's any need we can still give it to the witness at a later stage. Could the original be returned to the witness or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could -- I mean, he had it on -- I believe that the witness had in front of him during direct examination. If we could just check with the [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, do you have any problems in the Prosecution looking at your notes written on this? On your statement? What are the notes about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem. You can take a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Weber will return it to you after the break. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, I'm going start again. In paragraph 8 of your statement, you describe the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Romanija Brigade stating that it stretched from the Vrbanja bridge to the Slavisa Vajner Cica barracks. Is it also correct that your brigade's zone of responsibility extended to the east and included the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please repeat that for me? Did you say battalion or brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the brigade. Is it correct that your brigade's zone of responsibility extended to the east and included the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30697.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 1st Romanija Brigade Command report dated 23 June 1992 from, at that time, brigade commander, Colonel Dragomir Milosevic. The topic is the disposition of the brigade. If you could please just review the entire report - it's rather short - and let us know when you've done that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it correct that this report describes the zone of responsibility for the 1st Romanija Brigade and its battalions as they existed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of the positions of the brigade, where they were. I talked about the position of my company, in 1992, that was from the bridge to the bridge. And then the position of my battalion that was from Vrbanja Most, the bridge, to the Slavisa Vajner Cica barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. What battalion -- what battalions neighboured your battalions on each side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: We're the 2nd Battalion of the Sarajevo Brigade [as interpreted]. Next to us was the 1st Battalion, on the right. And to the left, there were parts of, I don't know...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't know if you finished your answer there or not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I just don't remember who was on our left. I just know that our line was up to the Slavisa Vajner Cica barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Does this document accurately describe the positions of your own battalion, the 3rd Battalion, at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that as a company commander you were responsible for knowing the positions of all the personnel under your command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Isn't it also correct, as a company commander, it was your -- it was your job to know the positions of any forces that could support your company in your immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that your battalion remained part of the 1st Romanija Brigade until early 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The headquarters of your company, the 1st Company, was in the former Drvorijeka shop in Grbavica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is correct that your battalion's headquarters was located on Banja Luka Street?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the war, the Pere Zdere - and I'm sorry for mispronouncing the name of the location - Pere Zdere restaurant was not far from your battalion's headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you spell it, Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so not as to rely on your pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The name I'm trying to pronounce is Pere, P-e-r-e, second word Zdere, Z-d-e-r-e.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for it to appear on the transcript so that the witness can look at it as well. You see it's written three lines from the bottom, now four lines, on the transcript: Pere Zdere. My pronunciation is most likely as bad as --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understand. Pere Zdere. There was no command close to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. How far was the battalion command from that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Over 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In 1993, is it correct that your battalion was made part of the 1st Sarajevo Brigade as the Smbr's 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that your battalion's zone of responsibility did not change after it was made part of the 1st Smbr?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender this document into evidence, 65 ter 30697.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30697 receives number P6538, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6538 is admitted. Mr. Weber, I intend to take a break in two or three minutes from now. If you have a few questions, please put them to the witness; if you would need more time for your next subject --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can go through a number of quick things and if Your Honours want to stop me whenever you would like, it's fine to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do it in three minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, until late 1992, is it correct your battalion commander was Radomir Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: First it was Brane Plakalovic, and after him Radomir Stojanovic. Brane, or Branislav, Plakalovic and then Radomir Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Stojanovic remained your battalion commander until late 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Aleksandar Petrovic became battalion commander in late 1992 or beginning of 1993, and Radomir Stojanovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. So just so we're clear, then, Aleksandar Petrovic succeeded Radomir Stojanovic as your battalion commander sometime toward the end of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know the exact dates of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No problem, sir. Is it correct that your battalion had two deputy commanders; those individuals were Milan Hrvacevic and Dragan Siljak, with a K, Siljak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a time. And then Hrvacevic was moved to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break now. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Zeljko Mitrovic was in charge of the work detail of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Until the end of 1993, is it correct that you were part of the command of the 2nd Battalion of the 1st Smbr?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: That would be it roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Once you became an assistant commander for security and intelligence, is it correct that you attended morning meetings with the battalion commander and the deputy commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that these meetings would take place at the battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Zeljko Mitrovic would attend these meetings; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you remember occasions where Mr. Mitrovic would attend the meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Well, possibly. Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try another individual. Is it correct that Nebojsa Ivkovic also attended the morning meetings of the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I think that he came from time to time to attend meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. How often would he attend the meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that during these meetings, you would discuss the personnel in the battalion and their deployments?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your own role as assistant commander for intelligence and security, is it correct that you continued to operate from the battalion headquarters on Banja Luka Street?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you became the assistant commander for security and intelligence, is it correct that your function required you to have detailed information on the security situation throughout the zone of responsibility of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you were an assistant commander, is it correct that the military police in your battalion were your responsibility, or they were under your authority?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No. We did not have any military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. As part of your role as a commander for security and intelligence, is it correct that you possessed the authority and you also had the obligation to detain or arrest any soldier suspected of committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution, please, have P06517, currently marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you is a list of names which you were previously shown during the Karadzic proceedings. During that case, at page 30847, you confirmed that this is a list of personnel at the 2nd Battalion Command on this first page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember some of the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Just so we're clear, is it correct that your commander's name appears at line number 19?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And your deputy commander, their names appear at numbers 8 and number 30; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct your name and signature appears at number 14?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the purpose of this list is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall any occasions that you signed lists while you were at the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Well, I see my signature here, but I really don't remember the purpose of this list. Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 31 of your statement, you state that there was a sniper squad at the battalion command directly subordinated to the commander. This would be Aleksandar Petrovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How do you know that the sniper squad existed and that it was subordinated to the battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: An order in the corps command said that sniper squads should be established. I can't remember when this was. And it was directly subordinated to the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of both versions. What I'll be referring to carries over onto page 4 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, on this page, we see two sections. One section is for the technical department, and the bottom section is for snipers. Under the sniper list, there are names of 11 individuals. These names include Nebojsa Ivkovic, Zlatko Subotic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll the list, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Zlatko Subotic and Marinko Krneta. Is it correct that these are the names of the sniper squad whom you referred to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: In my statement I said that I didn't remember the names of those people from the sniper squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, a second ago, I just asked you about Mr. Ivkovic. You indicated that he was present at some meetings of the battalion command. In this list, we see Mr. Ivkovic under the sniper section. Is it correct that he was, in fact, the commander of the battalion's sniper quad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I remember that Nebojsa Ivkovic was the commander of the signals squad in the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could tender this document at this time. I'm going to continue my line of questioning here after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document is already MFI'd under number P6517.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6517 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 19330.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you will be a signed statement provided by Milan Hrvacevic, one of the deputy commanders of your battalion. Mr. Hrvacevic provided this statement to the Sarajevo MUP on the 15th of March, 1996. If you could please look at the beginning of the statement, as can you see, your deputy commander describes his familiarity with the battalion's sniper squad. He mentions many of the names that were on the list that we just saw. My question: Could you explain to us how the deputy commander would be familiar with this information, and you, the assistant commander for security and intelligence, would not know the same information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Milan Hrvacevic was arrested after the Dayton Accord on the Fraternity and Unity bridge. He was beaten up. He provided statements -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir -- okay. It appears that Mr. Hrvacevic knows information related to the sniper squad. Could you explain to us how he would know and you not know the same information.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I can't explain. I told you I did not remember any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that you have no reason -- you have no factual knowledge of the matters that Mr. Hrvacevic is then discussing in this statement. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this statement, Mr. Hrvacevic states: "I emphasise that Zlatko Subotic and Marinko Krneta were known to be the best snipers of our battalion, and they acquired this reputation by actively taking part in sniper shooting." Are you claiming here today that you were not aware of this reputation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is what I'm claiming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be due to the English translation where it says "actively participated in opening sniper fire on buildings." I am reading the original B/C/S statement of this witness, where it is stated: "I would like to say that Zlatko Subotic and Marinko Krneta enjoyed the reputation as the best sniper shooters in our battalion. They acquired such an image as a result of their numerous activities and active participation in sniping activities." There's no reference to any buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look, then, at the question. I think that the question did not make any reference to buildings, so, therefore, perhaps it was the way in which it was translated or misunderstood. A human error. But, as it appears on the transcript, there seems to be no problem. And the witness has answered the question anyhow. You had no knowledge about their reputation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since have you no knowledge of this information, is it correct that you've reason to dispute these statements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: You mean Milan Hrvacevic's statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. Since you have no knowledge of the facts that Mr. Hrvacevic is discussing here, you have no reason to dispute these facts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Let me just say this briefly. I met up with Milan Hrvacevic after the war, perhaps five or six years later, I don't know exactly when, and he told me very briefly that when he was arrested, he provided a statement, that he had to sign all sorts of things under duress. He had been heavily beaten up and so on and so forth. This is as much as I know from a conversation with him. This is all he told me. He wouldn't go into any further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you did not see any of that yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this statement into evidence pursuant to Rule 89(C). The document is further supported by independent evidence, the list that was just previously admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to the admission of this statement. This statement was provided by a different witness before a different body during a different procedure. So far, our practice has been not to admit such statements into evidence in this particular way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, you are -- the Defence is not admitting anything, but I think the case law is that statements taken for the purposes of this Tribunal are not -- cannot be admitted unless Rule 92 bis or 92 ter are applied. But this is a statement taken by another authority. And if you could guide me, Mr. Stojanovic, where in the practice or the case law of this Tribunal the admission of such statements from the bar table are declared non-admissible, then I'd like to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- with your leave, this is a statement of which this witness has no knowledge. The only thing that he knows is that five or six years after the statement was taken from Hrvacevic, if it was, indeed, taken from him, under what conditions it had been taken. So there's no foundation for the admission of this statement through today's witness. Second of all, this statement was provided to the state organs, more specifically, to the police station in Sarajevo in March 1996. In no way is it suitable as evidence in this case. That is why we object to the admission of this statement into evidence. By the way, I am not able to give you the case law reference, but I believe in the Kosovo case and in the Popovic case, and with all due respect, we have been working so long in this case when I use statements from the Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, some of those statements were not deemed to be admissible in this case. That's why I'm objecting to the admission of Hrvacevic's statement through Maletic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. The parties have an opportunity to further -- to make further submissions, preferably in writing, on the admission of this document. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19330 receives number P6539, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it keeps that status for the time being. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if it assists, the main reason that we would be offering it is for -- as it goes to the witness's credibility that he was a position to know and he is claiming not to know of these individuals and someone similarly situated were. So if that assists counsel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I indicated that parties would have an opportunity to make further submissions, not at this moment orally. You have another three minutes for further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, you describe the enemy forces that opposed you. In paragraph 19, you state: "I know that my unit's counterpart on the opposite side was an HVO unit called Kralj Tvrtko. I was shown documents which I identified because, while I was the assistant for intelligence and security, I collected the initial information from the defectors." Is it correct that the Defence showed you documents according -- about this subject?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, it indicates that you describe an opposing HVO unit. You indicate that you were shown documents which you identified because "while I was the assistant for intelligence and security," you "collected the initial information from the defectors." Is it correct that the Defence showed you these documents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many documents you were shown?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall who the authors of the documents were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: I knew about the enemy side. I knew who was in front of our lines, and I heard that from the defectors. This is what I have stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could ask just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted to ask you this quickly before we finish for the day. We haven't had a full time to look at the statement that you had with you when you first came to court, but from an initial glance at it, there appears to be two different colour inks and possibly two different handwriting on it. Could you tell us, is there anyone else that wrote on that statement besides yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC
utterances.text: No. All of that is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn for the day. Witness, before you leave the courtroom, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever other way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given or still to be given tomorrow. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, according to my bookkeeping, you have 1 hour and 20 minutes left. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 29th of May, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of May, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
